answer:
Given data: Star-connected load, $V_L = 400\text{ V}$, $f = 50\text{ Hz}$, Wattmeter readings $W_1 = 3\text{ kW} = 3000\text{ W}$, $W_2 = 1\text{ kW} = 1000\text{ W}$.

**1. Total Power ($P$):**
$$P = W_1 + W_2 = 3000 + 1000 = 4000\text{ W}$$

**2. Power Factor Angle ($\phi$):**
$$\tan\phi = \sqrt{3} \frac{W_1 - W_2}{W_1 + W_2} = \sqrt{3} \frac{3000 - 1000}{3000 + 1000} = \sqrt{3} \frac{2000}{4000} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 0.866$$
$$\phi = \arctan(0.866) = 30^\circ$$
Power factor $\cos\phi = \cos(30^\circ) = 0.866\text{ lagging}$.

**3. Impedance per phase ($Z_{ph}$):**
Phase voltage $V_{ph} = \frac{V_L}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{400}{\sqrt{3}} = 230.94\text{ V}$
Total Power $P = 3 \cdot I_{ph}^2 R \implies 4000 = 3 \cdot \left(\frac{V_{ph}}{Z_{ph}}\right)^2 (Z_{ph} \cos\phi)$  *(since $R = Z_{ph}\cos\phi$)*
$$\frac{V_{ph}^2}{Z_{ph}} \cos\phi = \frac{4000}{3} \implies Z_{ph} = \frac{V_{ph}^2 \cos\phi}{1333.33} = \frac{(230.94)^2 \times 0.866}{1333.33} = 34.64\text{ }\Omega$$

**4. Resistance ($R$) and Inductance ($L$):**
$$R = Z_{ph} \cos\phi = 34.64 \times 0.866 = 30\text{ }\Omega$$
$$X_L = Z_{ph} \sin\phi = 34.64 \times \sin(30^\circ) = 34.64 \times 0.5 = 17.32\text{ }\Omega$$
$$L = \frac{X_L}{2\pi f} = \frac{17.32}{2 \times \pi \times 50} = 0.0551\text{ H} = 55.1\text{ mH}$$
proTip: In the two-wattmeter method, if one wattmeter reads negative, reverse the pressure coil connections and take that reading as negative in formulas.
